problem: Existing visual navigation methods (GNM, ViNT, NoMaD, CityWalker) optimize shortest-path and collision avoidance via imitation learning, ignoring social norms such as jaywalking or walking on lawns. VLM-based social reasoning is disconnected from low-level action generation.
motivation: Robots such as guide dogs need to be socially compliant, not just geometrically efficient. Behavior cloning does not capture the causal structure of norms, and RL without semantic priors struggles to discover compliant behaviors from sparse rewards.
key_idea: A hierarchical VLM 'brain' plus flow-matching action expert, trained on a 7M-sample cognition+trajectory dataset and then refined with SAFE-GRPO, a flow-based RL stage with a traversability-based social reward.
insight: Cognitive data (D_cog) is essential for RL to work. SAFE-GRPO without D_cog lowers DCR/TCR (68.1/66.9 vs 69.8/68.2 for IL alone), while with D_cog it raises them to 82.5/82.9. Data scaling helps step by step (video, sim, cog). Removing R_social drops DCR/TCR from 82.5/82.9 to 61.4/62.1, so the social reward drives compliance. RL costs slight SPL (79.4 to 77.4).
method: Brain Module: Qwen2.5-VL-3B that outputs socially traversable polygons, CoT explanations and VQA. Its last-layer latent features condition the action expert.
Action Expert: 12-layer Diffusion Transformer with conditional flow matching (5 denoising steps) that predicts 5 future 2D waypoints from 5 past monocular frames, positions and a goal point.

SocNav Dataset: 7M samples. Expert Trajectories Pyramid has 2.0M internet-video pseudo-trajectories (π3 + MoGe), 1.7M sim trajectories (SocialGS 3DGS, SocCity Isaac Sim, with recovery trajectories) and 340K real robot trajectories. The Cognitive Activation Dataset has 1.2M traversability annotations, 825K CoT samples from Qwen2.5VL-72B and 1M general VQA.
Three-stage training: (1) pre-train the full model on D_video, D_sim and D_cog; (2) fine-tune only the action expert on D_real; (3) SAFE-GRPO on SocCity.

SAFE-GRPO: converts the flow ODE to an SDE for exploration while the VLM latent stays fixed. Reward = R_social (distance-transform clearance vs expert on a semantic occupancy map) + expert similarity + smoothness + efficiency.
SocNav Benchmark: 9 new 3DGS scenes (73K m²) in Isaac Sim with a Unitree Go2, digital pedestrians, and 20 cases per scene. Adds DCR/TCR social compliance metrics.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-3B brain + 12-layer Diffusion Transformer flow action expert (trained/fine-tuned)
setting.training_data: SocNav Dataset: 7M samples (2.0M internet-video pseudo-trajectories, 1.7M simulated trajectories, 340K real robot trajectories, 1.2M traversability, 825K CoT, 1M VQA); RL on SocCity trajectories
setting.observation: history of 5 monocular RGB frames + 2D positions + 2D goal point
setting.action_space: predicted 2D waypoint chunks (5 steps) executed by a locomotion policy
setting.privileged: none at test time (GT occupancy map used only in RL reward during training)

numbers.extra: all 3 stages incl. SAFE-GRPO; 9 unseen 3DGS scenes, 20 cases each

numbers.evidence: Table 1 Open-Loop Evaluation on CityWalker Benchmark

numbers.eval_set_note: 20 trials in each of 3 environments (street crossing, office park, shopping mall)
numbers.extra: Unitree Go2, A10 cloud server, >5 Hz

results: On the closed-loop SocNav Bench SocialNav reaches SR 86.1, SPL 77.4, DCR 82.5 and TCR 82.9, versus CityWalker's SR 47.8, SPL 44.7, DCR 36.1 and TCR 36.6 (+38.3 SR). It also gets the lowest MAOE on the CityWalker open-loop benchmark (10.2 vs 15.2) and 85% real-world SR vs 62.5% for CityWalker.
limitations: Reward is hand-crafted and limited to semantic traversability; other context-dependent norms are not covered.
Slight SPL drop after RL, since compliant paths are less direct.
Social compliance is measured only by traversable-region occupancy (DCR/TCR) in a self-built benchmark, with baselines retrained on D_real.
